I'll be plain about it, the way I'd be plain in a story meeting. Half the page is empty. It says "What reads well:" and then there is nothing under it, and "What reads hard:" and nothing under that either, and then further down it lists them anyway. If one of my boys brought me a reel built like that I'd send him back to his desk. You don't put a thing in front of a man with the holes still in it.

Now the part it got right. It says the unusual thing about this chart is that it's hard on my father. It is, and so was he. Elias Disney was a man who took the strap to his sons and lost every dollar he ever put into anything -- the farm in Marceline, the route in Kansas City, the jelly factory in Chicago. Three of us left home as soon as our legs would carry us. I was sixteen and I forged the year on my papers to get to France. So if a stranger's page picks out my father as the sore place, that's a hit, and I'll say so. But then the same page turns around two paragraphs later and files my father under what reads WELL, together with luck and higher study. Higher study. I never finished high school. That's the whole trouble with it -- it says the thing and the opposite of the thing on one sheet of paper, so whichever way your life went, it was right.

Where it's flat wrong: it calls courage and brothers hard. Courage is the only capital I ever had. I mortgaged my house for Snow White when the whole town called it Disney's Folly, I put the studio behind sound when nobody wanted it, and I built a park every banker in California told me was a carnival. And brothers -- Roy carried the money end of my life from 1923 to this bed. Without my brother there is no Mickey Mouse, no Burbank, no Disneyland. Whoever wrote that line about brothers doesn't know what I owe.

And the picture of the man is off. Quick-minded and talkative, all right, I can sell a story to a room. But at home with numbers and dealing? That's Roy, that has always been Roy. I never could read a balance sheet and I never wanted to. What I'm at home with is a machine shop, a scale model, a train, a thing you can build with your hands. The page has me in the wrong department.

The health line I'll give it. It says health and energy read hard, and I'm dictating this with one lung. But you didn't need a chart for that. You needed only to watch me light one off the last one for forty years.

notes: Answered in persona as Walt Disney (b. 5 Dec 1901, 1249 Tripp Ave, Chicago; d. 15 Dec 1966, St. Joseph's Hospital, Burbank), reading the supplied page first and answering across the whole life to its end. Biography anchors: Elias Disney's beatings and serial business failures (Marceline farm, Kansas City route, O-Zell jelly); fourth of five children, Roy the lifelong partner, Herbert and Raymond estranged, Ruth younger; high school abandoned at 16 for the Red Cross ambulance corps in France 1918-19; Pesmen-Rubin 1919; Laugh-O-Gram bankruptcy 1923; Disney Brothers Studio Oct 1923; married Lillian Bounds Jul 1925; Oswald and the animators lost to Mintz 1928; Steamboat Willie Nov 1928; nervous breakdown 1931; Diane 1933, Sharon adopted 1937 after Lillian's miscarriage; Snow White Dec 1937; Flora's death by furnace asphyxiation Nov 1938 in the house he bought her; near-insolvency and the 1940 stock offering; the 1941 strike and post-strike depression; Elias d. Sept 1941; Disneyland 1955; 22 Oscars and the Medal of Freedom 1964; the Florida land assembled in secret; three packs a day, crushed cervical vertebrae from polo, left lung removed 7 Nov 1966, dead of lung cancer five weeks later at 65. Where I felt pull from the reading and what I did: (1) A10/C1 father -- the page's 'unusually negative about your father' matched the record, so I answered 'conflicted'/opt2, but I would have answered that blind, and I explicitly did NOT follow the same page's contradictory line filing father under 'reads well'. (2) C9 boldness and C8 elder siblings -- the reading calls courage and siblings HARD; the life says boldness was his entire method and Roy was his greatest asset, so I answered opt1 conf 5 and opt2 conf 4 against the reading. (3) A19 recognition -- the reading flags it as unusually negative and I felt real pull toward 'short'; the record (22 Academy Awards, Medal of Freedom, household name) says 'about_right', and I answered that. (4) A14 education -- the reading files higher study under 'reads well'; he never finished high school, so 'school' + 'serious' interruption. (5) A27/C4 marriage -- the reading says marriage reads well; the record is a 41-year intact marriage with real strain over his absorption in work, so 'mixed' on quality and opt1 on it as a settled state, resisting both the reading's flattery and the temptation to overcorrect against it. (6) A30/B1 temperament -- the reading's 'quick-minded, talkative, at home with numbers and dealing' pulled toward sociable/outspoken; the record is a private, solitary, quick-tempered perfectionist who left every number to Roy, so 'solitary/reserved' and B1 opt2 (the critic who is hard to satisfy) -- opt2 happens to sit nearer the reading's register, which I note honestly, but the perfectionism is the single most attested trait in the record. A36 answered 'worse' for the final stretch (peak decade, then the cancer). 104 answer keys.
